title: Prop 15.237 residual (ii-a) ND: dual-bad U is not a 0-1 pair-span function

B.theorem: Wedges: G=±1/p>−1+2/p. Disjoint: G₆≻0 (indep. of 6 pair features) ⇒ open PSD interval ⇒ G>−1+2/p. Hence P(f=f′=1)>0 and all four sign pairs occur.

D.theorem: L²=L + four quadrants: 0-1 pair-span functions are constants, pair-slices, or triangle 3-equals. None can be U_{-4,−}.

even_types.theorem: The 7 even types of {±1}^4 other than {all ±} already span R^6 under the 6 pair monomials (integer 7×6 matrix, rank 6).

disjoint_product.theorem: On the four sign pairs, f f′=a+b f+c f′ overdetermines: the first three pairs force (a,b,c)=(−1,1,1), the fourth needs 1=−3. Hence a disjoint product is not pair-span, so a 2-matching in supp(a) cannot satisfy L²=L.

support.theorem: An edge set with no 2-matching is a clique of pairwise adjacent edges: a triangle or a star (including 0–1 edges). Any 4-edge subset of K4 contains a matching; path-3 does too.

wedge_p5.theorem: Wedge G=±1/p (15.48, Max− opposite to Max+). −1/p>−1+2/p ⇔ p>3.

triangle_pd_p5.theorem: Triangle pair Gram: diag 1, off ±1/p; eigs 1+2/p, 1−1/p (×2).

three_equal_SH.theorem: If 1_U is a triangle 3-equal, the unique expansion in the PD triangle Gram gives 2(S+f_e)+7+∑ε f_tri=0, so S_H=(−7−∑ε f)/2. 3-equal is |∑ε f|=3, hence S_H∈{−5,−2}. Dual-bad needs S_H∈{−5,−3}.
